_note: Config for emit_summit_matrix.py — the SUMMIT side of estMatrix (the model's own estimates per snapshot). The consensus side has its own map_<tk>.json / valid_<tk>.json.
_derived_note: Uber's model has no total-GB row; the dataset's `gb` is Mobility + Delivery + Freight, exactly as gb.act reconciles to each release (see the header note in js/results-data/uber.js).
_decimals_note: EPS keeps 4 decimals like the consensus matrix; everything else is US$ millions / counts in millions at 1 decimal, matching the hand-authored summit arrays.
_vintages_note: The five usable model snapshots. Deduped by facts_hash (2026-05-06 == 2026-05-07); 2026-07-17 and 2026-08-03 are intra-period saves; 2026-07-20 is unusable (Delivery-Hero pro-forma toggle ON). lastActual = the last period REPORTED when that file was saved.
_views_note: Which dataset metric keys get a matrix row per view. Order here is the order emitted. ANNUAL trips and fcf are deliberately absent: the model's annual ORDERS row is on the audit list (FY2026 reads 12,260 against a 13,567 FY2025 ACTUAL) and annual FCF carries two competing rows (see prefer_source). The quarterly rows of both are sound. Leaving them out keeps the matrix from re-introducing the exact numbers the dataset chose to null out.
_prefer_source_note: Some rows exist twice under different `source` tags. Annual FCF is the live case: DEFAULT reads 11,338 for FY2026 where SEGM reads 10,665 (the segment build-up). SEGM is the one the quarterly rows already reconcile to, so it wins; the emitter reports every conflict it resolves.
_axis_note: The dataset's period axis — cells outside it are dropped so the matrix never carries a period the metric cannot plot.
